en.title: Fraction Farms
en.basics_denominator_01: Here at Fraction Farms, we showcase how to divide up land in order to produce crops more efficiently.
en.basics_denominator_02: We do this by taking Unit Tiles and breaking their sides into fractional lengths.
en.basics_denominator_03: For each side, there is a back and forward button to change the number of parts each side is divided up by.
en.basics_denominator_04: Let's use them to divide up this piece of farm land. Click the submit button to check your results.
en.basics_denominator_05: Excellent! Let's try a different combination.
en.basics_numerator_01: Good job! Now, we need to identify the portion of land we want to use now that it is divided.
en.basics_numerator_02: We use the side buttons to highlight a portion of tiles.
en.basics_numerator_03: We then need to click on the individual pieces that intersect with the highlighted portions.
en.basics_numerator_04: Click submit once you think you have selected the right number of tiles.
en.basics_multiply_01: You're a fast learner! Great job!
en.basics_multiply_02: Notice how the solution we are getting is the same as if we multiplied the fractions together, multiplying the numerators togehter and the denominators together.
en.basics_multiply_05: Wonderful! You've mastered working with one tile, but dividing up land sometimes takes multiple tiles.
en.basics_multiply_06: Let's move onto another part of the farm!
en.basics_error_01: Use the back and forward buttons on each side in order to get the land divided up correctly.
en.basics_error_02: Click on the individual tiles to accumulate the right portion of land.
en.basics_error_03: If you're having a hard time, don't forget you can multiply the numerators and denominators together and use that as a guide.
en.mixed_line_01: We need more than one tile when were dealing with numbers greater than one.
en.mixed_line_02: Working with multiple tiles is easy, though. You just need to click on the tile you want to interact with to enable it.
en.mixed_line_03: We can still count up the tiles, but because we are dealing with mixed tiles of fractional size, we show the answer with the common denominator.
en.mixed_line_05: Great job! Notice how the same rule applies, that we get the same solution had we multiplied the two numbers together.
en.mixed_line_07: Good job! Keep it up! You're doing great!
en.mixed_line_09: I'm impressed! You've done really well to come this far.
en.mixed_line_10: You know, there is another way we can look at these problems that reference back to when we used one tile. Come on, I'll show you!
en.mixed_error_01: Remember to divide up the tiles using the forward and back buttons.
en.mixed_error_02: Use the highlighting to find the intersection of the two fractional lengths.
en.mixed_error_03: Don't forget, if you're having problems, don't be afraid to multiply the numbers together.
en.improper_line_01: Another way we can visualize using multiple tiles is by slicing up all the tiles by the same denominators, and counting the individual tiles up together.
en.improper_line_02: This will require us to look at our fractions as improper fractions. Let's take the problem we just completed and do it again, but looking at it as improper fractions.
en.improper_line_03: Well done! Now, on your own, convert the problem to improper fractions and solve the next problems using this method.
en.improper_line_04: Nicely done! Let's try the next one!
en.improper_line_05: Excellent! Just one more to go.
en.improper_line_06: Bravo! You've become quite the expert at being able to divide up land.
en.improper_line_07: I think you're ready to try dividing up not just the land, but manage multiple crops that we need to produce. Let's go to the last land plot!
en.improper_error_01: Remember to convert the mixed fractions into improper fractions. Don't be afraid to multiply the fractions together if you're having trouble.
